children: Heritage Foods Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19 per cent to Rs 1,319.6 crore, while Pat fell 39 per cent amid higher milk procurement costs

Heritage Foods  reported a 19 per cent year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 1,319.6 crore in the second quarter of FY27, supported by growth in milk sales and value-added products. However, profit after tax (Pat) fell 39 per cent to Rs 30.9 crore amid an 11 per cent rise in milk procurement prices, while the Ebitda margin recovered 98 basis points sequentially to 5.6 per cent.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated revenue grew 18 per cent YoY to Rs 2,657.7 crore, while Pat declined 39 per cent to Rs 55.8 crore, reflecting continued pressure on profitability.

Milk procurement volumes rose 7 per cent YoY to 17.28 lakh litres per day (LLPD) in the July-September quarter. However, the average landed procurement price increased 11 per cent to Rs 47.73 per litre, driven by sustained demand and higher feed costs.
Milk sales volumes grew at a slower pace of 2.5 per cent YoY to 12.35 LLPD during the quarter. The average selling price, meanwhile, increased 6 per cent to Rs 60.34 per litre.

Revenue from value-added products (VAP), excluding ghee and butter, increased 32 per cent YoY to Rs 451 crore in Q2 FY27. The segment's contribution to revenue, excluding ghee and butter, rose to 35.4 per cent from 31.3 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year.

Lassi led category growth with a 91 per cent increase, followed by ice cream at 81 per cent, buttermilk at 66 per cent, paneer at 38 per cent and curd at 26 per cent. The increase in VAP contribution indicates a shift towards higher-value dairy categories, although the company's overall profitability remained under pressure from rising milk procurement costs.

Brahmani Nara, Executive Director of Heritage Foods, said the company delivered 19 per cent YoY revenue growth and a 98 basis points sequential recovery in Ebitda margin to 5.6 per cent, despite elevated milk procurement costs.
Nara added that the company's focus remains on strengthening the procurement ecosystem, expanding VAP capacity and accelerating innovation across premium and nutrition-led categories.
